CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steve Talt, Mayor  www.CityofSanMarino.org
Steven W. Huang, DDS, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Tony Chou, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 11, 2023 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108
  AND
  NO. 56, PINGDING RD., UNIT 56-7, 11TH FLOOR
  TAMSUI DISTRICT, NEW TAIPEI CITY, TAIWAN 251

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with  valuable  information  regarding  issues  of  the  community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned  meetings are held  on  the last  Friday of every month  at  8:30  a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at (626)
300-0705  prior  to  the  meeting  for  assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do  it’s  best  to  resolve  any  technical  issues  as  quickly  as  possible.

 How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Via Computer for Video Streaming:
  Website: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/83316497270
  Meeting ID: 833 1649 7270
  Via Phone for Audio Only:
  Phone Number: (669) 900-9128
  Meeting ID: 833 1649 7270

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org until 3:00
  p.m. the day of the meeting, to be read by the City Clerk during public comment.
  Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the interest of time, and previously
  distributed public comment will be noted. Any comments received after 3:00 p.m. will
  be included in the public comment record but will not be read at the meeting.
  Public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module
  during the meeting. Zoom comments will be taken after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Huang, and Mayor Talt

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At this
time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda. Pursuant
to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the meeting
agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place limits on
duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

AGENDA – OCTOBER 11, 2023  PAGE 2 of 6
 CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having to
read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on First Reading
must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not require having the
title read. However, the City Council may request that an ordinance or resolution be read in
its entirety before taking any action.

  CONTINUED BUSINESS

 1.  PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. O-
  23-1407 (FIRST READING) AMENDING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS
  23.02.14 AND 23.15.04.1 TO ALLOW MINISTERIAL APPROVAL WHEN
  RECONFIGURING SPACE WITHIN AN EXISTING DWELLING UNIT IN
  THE SINGLE-FAMILY (R-1) ZONE TO CREATE NO MORE THAN TWO
  ADDITIONAL BEDROOMS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Ordinance No. O-23-1407. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to waive full reading and introduce by title only Ordinance No. O-23- 1407, an
  Ordinance of the San Marino City Council amending San Marino Municipal Code
  Sections 23.02.14 and 23.15.04.1 to implement Assembly Bill 916 by allowing
  ministerial approval when reconfiguring space within an existing residential dwelling
  unit in the single-family (R-1) zone to create no more than two additional bedrooms.”

  NEW BUSINESS

 2.  RECEIVE AND FILE FINANCIAL REPORT FOR FOURTH QUARTER
  (APRIL 2023 THROUGH JUNE 2023)

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the financial report reflecting the City’s revenues and
  expenditures as of June 30, 2023.”

AGENDA – OCTOBER 11, 2023  PAGE 3 of 6
 3.  APPROVAL OF FY 2022-23 BUDGET CARRYOVERS AND FY 2023-24
  RE-BUDGETS AND FINAL FY 2022-23 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the requested FY
  2022-23 carryovers, updates to the FY 2023-24 re-budgets, and the budget
  amendments to the funds and accounts as noted on the attachments. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the requested FY 2022-23 carryovers, updates to the FY 2023-24
  re-budgets, and the budget amendments to the funds and accounts as noted on the
  attachments in the Staff Report.”

4.  CONSIDERATION OF 4TH AMENDMENT TO ATHENS CONTRACT TO
  ALLOW FOR NEGOTIATIONS OF A NEW OR AMENDED CONTRACT TO
  CONFORM TO SB 1383; APPROVE AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH
  ECONOMICS FOR WASTE FRANCHISE NEGOTIATION CONSULTING
  SERVICES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the 4th
  Amendment to the Agreement with Athens and authorize the City Manager to execute
  an amendment to the contract with Economics to increase the maximum expenditure
  amount from $30,000 to $210,000 to accommodate the necessary negotiations. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the 4th Amendment to Agreement with Athens, authorize the City
  Manager to execute an amendment to the contract with Economics to increase the not
  to exceed amount to $210,000, and authorize an additional appropriation of $125,000
  into Account #101-40-4104-0000 from the General Fund Reserves as part of the FY
  2023-24 budget.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Council approve the minutes of the
  regular meeting of September 13, 2023, the joint City Council and Recreation
  Commission meeting of September 29, 2023, and the adjourned regular meeting of
  September 29, 2023. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate  motion  would  be:

  “I move to approve the minutes of the regular meeting of September 13, 2023, the
  joint meeting with the Recreation Commission of September 29, 2023, and the
  adjourned regular meeting of September 29, 2023.”

6.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF AUGUST 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

AGENDA – OCTOBER 11, 2023  PAGE 4 of 6
   “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of August
  2023.”

7.  RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR
  SEPTEMBER 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of September 2023. If the City Council concurs
  with  staff’s recommendation,  an  appropriate  motion  would  be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of
  September 2023.”

8.  COMMITMENT OF DONATIONS FUND YEAR-END BALANCE RESERVES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the accompanying
  resolution to commit the balance as of June 30, 2023 as noted in the attachments. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-23-26 to commit the balance of $245,604 in the
  Donations Fund as of June 30, 2023.”

9.  AUTHORIZATION  OF  MEMORANDUM  OF  AGREEMENT  AND
  APPROPRIATION OF ADDITIONAL BUDGET FOR CONTINUED
  PARTICIPATION IN COYOTE MANAGEMENT PLAN AND INCREASING
  THE  ANNUAL  CONTRIBUTION  FROM  $10,000 TO  $10,600

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council authorize the City Manager to
  execute the Second Amendment to the Memorandum of Understanding with the San
  Gabriel Valley Council of Governments for participation in the Coyote Management
  Implementation  Plan.

  If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to authorize the City Manager to execute the Second Amendment to the
  Memorandum of Understanding with the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments
  for participation in the Coyote Management Implementation Plan, extending the term
  through June 30, 2025 increasing the annual contribution from $10,000 to $10,600,
  and appropriate an additional $600 to account #101-09-4150-0000 for the increase
  for contracted services.”

10. APPROVAL OF PURCHASE OF BACKHOE FOR PARKS AND PUBLIC
  WORKS DEPARTMENT FROM JOHN DEERE AND APPROPRIATION OF
  $1,317.35 FROM THE CAPITAL EQUIPMENT FUND RESERVES FOR THE
  PURCHASE

AGENDA – OCTOBER 11, 2023  PAGE 5 of 6
   Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the purchase of one
  backhoe from John Deere in the amount of $71,317.35, and authorize the
  appropriation of $1,317.35 from the Capital Equipment Fund reserves into Account #
  591-48-4613-0000  (Capitalized  Equipment).

  “I move to approve the purchase of one backhoe from John Deere in the amount of
  $71,317.35, and authorize the appropriation of $1,317.35 from the Capital Equipment
  Fund reserves into Account # 591-48-4613-0000 (Capitalized Equipment).”

 11. ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. O-23-1406 (SECOND READING)
  ADDING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.06.16 TO IMPLEMENT STATE
  LAW REGARDING PARKING REQUIREMENTS WITHIN A HALF-MILE
  OF PUBLIC TRANSIT

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Ordinance No. O-23-1405. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to adopt Ordinance No. O-23- 1406, an Ordinance of the San Marino City
  Council adding San Marino Municipal Code Section 23.06.16 to implement Assembly
  Bill 2097 by eliminating minimum parking requirements on a residential, commercial,
  or other development project if the project is located within one-half mile of public
  transit.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

ADJOURNMENT

  CITY CLERK
